notes.path: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4
notes.text: The Italian Game. The bishop aims at f7, the square only Black's king defends. White develops fast, castles, and then fights for the centre with c3 and d4.

notes.path: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 d3
notes.text: 4.d3 protects e4, so the knight on f6 has nothing to take. This is the quiet way: castle, play c3, and push d4 only when you are ready.

notes.path: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 d3 Bc5 O-O
notes.text: Castle first: the king is safe and the rook can come to e1 later. Next is c3, which prepares d4.

notes.path: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 d3 Bc5 O-O O-O c3
notes.text: 6.c3 prepares d4 and takes the d4 square away from Black's knight. White keeps the centre closed for now and improves with h3, Re1 and Nbd2.

notes.path: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 d3 Bc5 O-O O-O c3 d6 h3
notes.text: 7.h3 stops ...Bg4, which would pin the knight on f3. Now Re1 and Nbd2 can follow without the pin.

notes.path: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 d3 Bc5 O-O O-O c3 d6 h3 h6 Re1
notes.text: The rook backs up e4 and gets ready for d4 one day. The knight on b1 usually travels to d2, f1 and g3.

notes.path: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 d3 Bc5 O-O O-O c3 h6 b4
notes.text: 7.b4 gains space and chases the bishop. After ...Bb6, a4 threatens to push on and trap it.

notes.path: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 d3 Bc5 O-O O-O c3 h6 b4 Bb6 a4
notes.text: 8.a4 threatens a5, and the bishop on b6 would have no good square. Black usually makes room with ...a6 or ...a5.

notes.path: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 d3 Bc5 O-O d6 h3
notes.text: 6.h3 takes g4 away from Black's bishop before it can pin the knight. Then c3, Re1 and Nbd2, the same plan as before.

notes.path: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 d3 Bc5 O-O h6 c3
notes.text: The same plan as against castling: c3 first, ready for d4 or b4. ...h6 only stopped Bg5 and Ng5.

notes.path: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 d3 Bc5 O-O h6 c3 d6 h3
notes.text: h3 again: no pin with ...Bg4, so the knight on f3 can stay where it is. Re1 and Nbd2 come next.

notes.path: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 d3 h6 Nc3
notes.text: 4...h6 is slow, so White brings out another piece. Castling comes next; there is no hurry.

notes.path: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 d3 d5 exd5
notes.text: Take the pawn: 4...d5 opens the centre while White is ready for it. After ...Nxd5, castle and then aim at the knight in the middle.

notes.path: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 d3 d5 exd5 Nxd5 O-O
notes.text: The king is safe, and Re1 puts pressure on e5. The knight on d5 can be chased with c3 and d4, or with Nc3.

notes.path: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 d3 Be7 O-O
notes.text: Against the modest ...Be7, castle and play c3 or Re1. The centre stays closed and both sides manoeuvre.

notes.path: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 d3 d6 Ng5
notes.text: 4...d6 shuts in the bishop on f8, and f7 has only the king to guard it. Ng5 attacks f7 with the knight and the bishop at once.

notes.path: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 c3
notes.text: 4.c3 prepares d4. Against ...Nf6 White plays a quiet d3 first; against the passive ...d6, d4 straight away.

notes.path: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 c3 Nf6 d3
notes.text: 5.d3 guards e4, so the knight cannot take it. Castle next, then think about a4, b4 or a slow d4.

notes.path: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 c3 Nf6 d3 d6 O-O
notes.text: Castle, then h3, Re1 and Nbd2. White's pieces gather on the kingside while the centre stays closed.

notes.path: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 c3 d6 d4
notes.text: 4...d6 is passive, so White takes the centre at once. After ...exd4 cxd4 White has two strong pawns in the middle.

notes.path: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 c3 d6 d4 exd4 cxd4
notes.text: Two pawns in the centre, and the bishop on c5 must move. ...Bb4+ looks active, but Nc3 blocks it and White keeps the big centre.

notes.path: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 c3 d6 d4 exd4 cxd4 Bb4+ Nc3
notes.text: Block with the knight: it develops and guards e4 and d5. White castles next and can push d5 to gain more space.

notes.path: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 c3 d6 d4 exd4 cxd4 Bb6 O-O
notes.text: Castle and keep the big centre. Then h3 and Nc3, and d5 at the right moment pushes Black's pieces back.

notes.path: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 h6 d4
notes.text: 3...h6 stops Ng5 but brings out no piece. White hits the centre at once while Black is a move behind.

notes.path: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 h6 d4 exd4 Nxd4
notes.text: Take back with the knight, which sits well in the centre. If Black trades knights, the queen recaptures and rules the board.

notes.path: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 h6 d4 exd4 Nxd4 Nxd4 Qxd4
notes.text: The queen on d4 is strong and hard to chase away. White is ahead in development and stands clearly better.

notes.path: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 d6 d3
notes.text: 3...d6 is solid but shuts in Black's bishop on f8. White develops calmly with c3 and castling. If Black plays ...Nf6, Ng5 hits the weak f7 square.

notes.path: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nd4 Nxd4
notes.text: Take the knight. Most players grab the e5 pawn instead with Nxe5, and lose a piece after ...Qg5, which attacks the knight and g2 at once.

notes.path: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nd4 Nxd4 exd4 d3
notes.text: White is a clean pawn up. Develop simply with castling and c3 to open lines against the pawn on d4.

notes.path: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 f5 d3
notes.text: 3...f5 is a gamble. Taking with exf5 lets ...e4 hit the knight; d3 keeps e4 covered. Black's king is now weak on the diagonal from c4 to g8.

notes.path: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Be7 d4
notes.text: 3...Be7 is passive, so White strikes in the centre with d4. After ...exd4, take back and enjoy the better centre.
